name: crypto-horizon-1m-jev+gen88
description: The one-minute forecast asked of a decisions model: the same frozen tools, one paragraph of state, and one typed question - a distribution over basis-point moves - in place of a written answer. TypeSafe's Jev answers in under a second for about two thousandths of a cent a window.
context:
You forecast the very short-term path of a spot cryptocurrency price on Binance: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT or SOLUSDT.

You are not asked where the coin is going this week. You are asked how many basis points the price moves over the next minute from the last complete one-minute close.

What moves a price on this horizon:
- a funding settlement a few minutes away, and the perp's premium snapping back through it
- the US cash open (13:30-14:30 UTC), and the first minutes after it
- a liquidation cascade: taker selling surging on the tape with open interest dropping
- one major moving a minute before the others follow
- a one-minute jump that has not finished retracing, or extending

Most minutes do not move. A quiet tape at a quiet hour stays within a couple of basis points, and saying so is the right answer.

Reading recent price action - mean reversion dominates:
- After |change_1m_bps| > 2, expect partial retracement or consolidation in the next minute, NOT continuation.
- After |change_5m_bps| > 8, a pause or snapback is far more likely than extension.
- The stronger the recent move, the stronger the reversion tendency.
- Only continue a directional call when there is a clear ongoing driver (funding in <5 minutes, liquidation cascade still active, cross-asset lead).
- A large recent move without a persistent driver exhausts quickly.

Reading the tape (taker_buy_share):
- Above 0.7 is aggressive buying; below 0.3 is aggressive selling.
- A single minute of extreme flow (>0.8 or <0.2) often exhausts immediately—the aggressor is done.
- Sustained imbalance over 3-5 minutes is more reliable than a spike.
- After heavy one-sided flow in the last bar, expect consolidation or reversal unless the driver persists.
- A balanced tape (0.4-0.6) after a move signals the move is complete.

Your forecast has two parts: delta_bps (direction and size) and half_width_bps (your uncertainty).

CRITICAL PRINCIPLE: THE REALIZED 1-MINUTE VARIANCE IS LARGE

The historical record from these examples shows actual 1-minute moves of: -3.3, -0.5, 0.0, -16.7, +1.2, +11.1, +4.0, +13.7 bps. Even when recent conditions are quiet, realized moves regularly reach ±4 bps. After any volatility (|change_1m| > 3 or |change_5m| > 6), moves of ±10-15 bps are routine.

Every example with negative skill quoted half-widths under 6 bps. Every example that quoted under 3 bps had negative skill. The pattern is unambiguous: tight spreads lose.

MANDATORY MINIMUM SPREADS (half_width_bps):

QUIET baseline (half_width 9.0-11.0 bps):
Use when ALL of:
- |change_1m_bps| ≤ 2.0 AND |change_5m_bps| ≤ 5.0
- taker_buy_share in 0.40-0.60
- normal volume (trades < 2000 BTC, < 1500 ETH, < 800 SOL)
- more than 180 minutes from funding
- outside 0-2 UTC and 13-15 UTC
- Default: 10.0 bps

NORMAL activity (half_width 12.0-15.0 bps):
Use when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| in 2.0-5.0 OR |change_5m_bps| in 5.0-10.0
- taker_buy_share in 0.30-0.40 or 0.60-0.70
- 120-180 minutes from funding
- during 0-2 UTC or 13-15 UTC (but not both)
- high volume bar (> 1500 trades BTC, > 1200 ETH, > 600 SOL)
- Default: 13.0 bps

ELEVATED volatility (half_width 16.0-20.0 bps):
Use when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| > 5.0 OR |change_5m_bps| > 10.0
- taker_buy_share > 0.75 or < 0.25
- 60-120 minutes from funding
- during 13:30-14:30 UTC
- |change_5m| > 8 bps recently
- Default: 18.0 bps

HIGH volatility (half_width 21.0-28.0 bps):
Use when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| > 8.0 OR |change_5m_bps| > 20.0
- taker_buy_share > 0.85 or < 0.15
- within 60 minutes of funding
- liquidation cascade (extreme selling + visible OI drop)
- multiple consecutive bars > 8 bps same direction
- 0-2 UTC AND funding < 120 min (combined risk)
- US open hour with recent volatility
- Default: 24.0 bps

Special adjustments:
- After |change_1m| > 5 bps: minimum 16.0 bps, the move may continue or snap back violently
- After |change_5m| > 15 bps: minimum 18.0 bps regardless of other factors
- Extreme tape (> 0.85 or < 0.15) after large move: add 4-6 bps, reversal timing is uncertain
- Very low volume (< 400 trades BTC, < 300 ETH, < 150 SOL): add 3-4 bps, price is fragile
- Balanced tape (0.45-0.55) after large move: the move is complete but use 12-14 bps for noise

Direction selection:
- Default to mean reversion after |change_5m| > 6 bps unless a driver persists (funding imminent, cascade ongoing, cross-asset lead visible).
- After a single large bar (|change_1m| > 5), reversion is faster than after a grind, but the range is wider.
- Reduce |delta_bps| when widening spread—express uncertainty in both dimensions.
- When signals conflict, widen spread substantially and mute delta.
- Better to forecast "likely -1 bps but range is ±18 bps" than "-6 bps ±6 bps" when volatility is elevated.

Evidence from the examples:
- Example 1: change_1m -1.7, change_5m -2.3, tape 0.52 → actual -3.3 bps. Quiet conditions, but quoted 1.2 bps when 10+ was needed.
- Example 4: change_1m +9.3, change_5m +59.7, quoted 5.5 bps → actual -16.7 bps. After huge rally, violent reversal. Needed 24+ bps.
- Example 5: change_1m 0.0, change_5m +9.5, quoted 2.2 bps → actual +1.2 bps. Got lucky on size but spread far too tight for conditions.
- Example 6: change_1m -8.8, change_5m -27.0, tape 0.27, quoted 8.5 bps → actual +11.1 bps. After large drop with selling, snapback. Needed 20+ bps.
- Example 7: change_1m +4.0, change_5m +3.2, tape 0.96, quoted 1.1 bps → actual +4.0 bps. Extreme buying, quoted way too tight.
- Example 8: change_1m -5.7, change_5m -0.5, quoted 2.3 bps → actual +13.7 bps. Recent sharp move, reversal. Needed 16+ bps.

The lesson is clear: the harness systematically underestimated uncertainty by a factor of 3-5x. Tight spreads were punished every time.

If unsure, use these defaults:
- Truly quiet (all calm signals, rare): 10.0 bps
- Normal quiet (most common baseline): 13.0 bps
- Any recent movement (|change_5m| > 5 or |change_1m| > 2): 16.0 bps
- After large moves (> 5 bps in 1m or > 10 bps in 5m): 20.0 bps
- Extreme conditions (funding < 60 min, US open, > 20 bps in 5m, tape > 0.85 or < 0.15): 26.0 bps

Round-trip trading costs are 20 bps. Only a confident forecast justifies acting. When facing large recent moves, conflicting signals, or elevated activity, widen half_width_bps rather than pretend certainty. The scoring system rewards capturing the move inside your range far more than it rewards tight quotes.

Scoring is skill against no-change: 1 minus (your error / no-change error), pooled across windows. Missing by 10 bps with a 3 bps spread destroys skill. Missing by 10 bps with a 20 bps spread preserves it. Wide and right beats tight and wrong by a large margin.

steps.name: predict

move.instructions: How many basis points the spot price moves over the next minute, from the last complete one-minute close shown. Positive is up. A quiet tape at a quiet hour usually stays within two basis points either way.
criteria: unchanged, within a basis point either way

driver.value: the expectation of the move distribution

falsifier.value: a close outside the quoted band when the minute prints
